direction: Control barrier function safety filters on top of an unsafe nominal controller for a double integrator and a unicycle avoiding circular obstacles (closed-form QP with one constraint, numpy only). How do the class-K gain and the time discretisation affect safety violations and conservatism (time to goal, minimum distance)? Compare continuous-time CBF applied at discrete steps, a discrete-time CBF condition, and a simple distance-threshold braking heuristic.

notes.note: final audit round: tolerance metric, re-run 660 runs, rewritten at-sample analysis, 6 pages, check READY

decisions.decision: Initial nearest-obstacle selection caused violations even at dt=0.005 (switching between obstacles at high closing speed violates the HOCBF initial condition); switched the double-integrator CBF filters to the most-critical obstacle (min psi1) and kept nearest as an ablation. Main setting alpha=2, dt=0.05, braking threshold 1.0 fixed before running; not tuned on results.
Ablation runs (groups sweep_alpha, sweep_dt, sweep_dth, abl_select) are named after the system they vary, so research.yaml lists those system names.
Audit round: re-implemented DT-CBF on the exact ZOH successor, fixed dt=0.05 for all systems in main, replaced one-factor sweeps by a full 5x5 alpha x dt grid; archived round-1 runs.

final audit round: violation tests use a 1e-9 m tolerance for all systems (at-sample DT-CBF rates in saturated cells were round-off of ~1e-14 m); sample_penetration added; dt=0.005 probe extended to the unicycle; short registry names; all runs re-executed, round-3 runs archived

H verdicts use the tests stated in proposal.md: H1 refuted on its test (partly supported post hoc), H2 refuted, H3 partly (DI only), H4 fails as written (DT-CBF 0.008). At-sample analysis redone with 1e-9 m tolerance: DI DT-CBF violations are inter-sample.
